describes: Window glass, the panes of every window: old drawn glass, a little wavy, reflecting the sky and the town round it; behind it the room, by day lit from its window, and where a room is lit, the room by its lamp (its walls, ceiling and floor, its lamp, the curtains at the window).

notes.room: A room of the period behind every lit window (inf., to check against the survey photos when they come): papered walls in warm light tones, a white ceiling, a lacquered pine floor, a dark sofa or sideboard against the back wall, one incandescent lamp (about 2700 K) in a fabric shade hung half a metre under a ceiling of 2.4 m, the sill 0.8 m over the floor; white sheer side curtains and a valance just behind the glass. Its light makes the pane's depth: brighter and creamier near the lamp, deeper amber at the floor, the corners and the furniture. lampPower, lampSoftM2 (how close to the lamp its light stops rising), the corners' light and the shade's glow were judged by look. Where the furniture stands and where the lamp hangs are each window's seed, claiming nothing.
notes.daylight: An unlit room by day, as a share of the light on the window's face, through the glass in and out (`transmit`, a single pane: every glazed window in the street is putty-glazed in one pane, 108's cross windows remade as the 1901 ones in 1985 and 109's six-pane casements of 1850; a 1960s sealed pane would have four faces). Each surface is lit by how much of its sky the window fills (its form factor: about a fifth on the floor just inside, a thirtieth at a back wall 3.6 m in, little on the side walls and ceiling beside the glass, which see it edge on) and by what it sees through it, the street's view out against the light on the face (OS_Glass Reflected: a back wall sees the far shore and the water at about a quarter of it, the floor just inside the brighter sky), and only through the glass: the frame, post and bars take the rest of the hole (house.json glass.share, the windows' glassArea: 108 0.61, 109 0.47). `bounce` is the room's own light per square metre of glass, the internally reflected component of BRE Digest 310 (Hopkinson, Longmore and Petherbridge 1954): 0.85 W / (A (1 - R)) (C Rfw + 5 Rcw) % of the sky's horizontal light, for this room's 60.5 m2 at R 0.54 (walls 0.58, ceiling 0.82, floor 0.17), Rfw 0.42 and Rcw 0.70 about the window's middle 1.5 m up, C 35.6 for the far shore's 9 degrees: 0.57 % a square metre, against a face that takes half the horizontal light (the hemisphere's equator, half its zenith; a CIE overcast sky gives a wall 0.40 and the ground's bounce the rest). Sheer white curtains at the glass return about half the light that reaches them. In place of a room lit by the face's whole light through the whole hole (r02), which put 108's room alone at L19 at the street stop beside ref 10 (panes L* 6 to 18, its wall 87).
notes.wave: Drawn and cylinder glass before float glass (1960s) is never flat: its waves tilt it by about half a degree, a few waves a metre, enough to bend a straight edge in what it reflects (round 3, judged by look).
notes.curtains: share is of the hole's half width: the frame and the sash's stiles take its outer quarter or so, so at 0.3 the side curtains hung behind the frame, and at 0.34 each shows as a pale band a few centimetres wide along its jamb, and the valance (valanceShare, of the height) as one along the head: curtains drawn back to the sides under a short valance, so the glass between is the dark room (r04; at 0.5 and 0.16 they filled half of every pane and the top lights, and the window read as a pale grey, L50 beside its wall's 66 at the street stop, r03 critic). They hang only where a household lives and keeps the house: a type its keeper lives in (paints.json livedIn) and not boarded (house.py glass_digest); a warehouse's or a boarded house's panes show the bare room.

kinds.describes: The glass of a pane by the year it was glazed (fronts-windows-and-signs.md section 1): crown to about 1840, blown cylinder to 1928, machine-drawn sheet to the late 1960s, float after. Each bends what it reflects its own way: crown in rings about the disc's centre, cylinder in long waves with no pattern, drawn in waves one way only, float not at all. tiltDeg is the waves' largest tilt; perM the waves a metre, least and most.
